brief.description: Dedicated single-pan cast-iron cooking hob on an open iron stand, with continuous front heat dial and original 64px-per-block materials
brief.purpose: Sensory timing and heat tradeoff prototype; player serves a reserved batch
brief.silhouette: Shallow upper coal burner housing, four slender iron legs and low bracing; exposed skillet; no oven cavity or oven door
brief.bounds: 16x16 footprint; burner housing y=9..14, cooktop y=14..14.5; pan rim y=17.1; open lower stand
brief.materials: Quiet charcoal cast iron with face-specific cover seams and steel fasteners; dark seasoned skillet with a worn lip and clean cooking well; subdued directional steel supports; brass dial only
brief.interfaces: Ingredient menu; continuous rotary drag and arrow fine adjustment; crouch-scroll heat and crouch-use serving
brief.states: Empty, pale through golden through browned/charred food; continuous pointer rotation; lit fire
brief.construction: Native legal static Java cuboids; dynamic food and pointer rendered by block entity
brief.invariants: One visible skillet and one continuous dial at existing coordinates, one batch and existing coal use; no oven door, no baking function; cooking cues, timing and reduced room heat retained
brief.technological_stage: Experimental Tier 2 cookware and manual coal-fired regulation
brief.material_behavior: Quiet large iron planes with subtle 64px clusters; purposeful sharp seams and edge wear, no granite-like pits or brown rusty cookware. Ordered construction detail dominates random-looking texture.
brief.signature_feature: Exposed pan food colors with continuous front dial
brief.neighboring_assets: T1 Cooking Stove, dedicated Baking Oven in T2 kitchen concept, prepared Vegetable Skillet portion

fidelity_targets.burner: 16-wide upper housing, 5 units high, above an open lower stand; top remains y=14.5
fidelity_targets.stand: Four 1.5-unit square iron legs with low braces; large visible negative space under heating head
fidelity_targets.pan: 11-wide square skillet, firmly supported, rim y=17.1 and short handle to cook right

generations.prompt: Create a single Minecraft/Blockbench Java-cuboid style stove prototype, front three-quarter view, neutral grey background. Reference 1 gives Civilization kitchen materials and cookware, reference 2 gives the existing dark cast-iron stove body. Keep one compact one-block cast-iron body, short feet, small front coal fire door and ONE clearly accessible round heat dial at upper right. One shallow square cast-iron skillet sits firmly on top with thick raised rim and one short handle to the right; diced potato and carrot visibly fill the pan. No oven window, no extra instruments, no chimney or surrounding brickwork. Stove body 16 units wide, 14 units high, pan spans 11 units at height 16. Iron is charcoal grey with restrained seams and steel highlights; small brass dial pointer only. Native legal cuboid geometry, economical pixel material clusters. This is a playable continuous-heat control and exposed-food timing prototype; no glowing copper, no floating pieces, no logos or text. Show the whole object with pan contents visible from normal standing height.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Produce one coherent Minecraft/Blockbench concept render for the Civilization cooking stove redesign, neutral gray backdrop, whole object front three-quarter view. Reference 1 is the previous in-game stove: preserve its compact one-block footprint, square open skillet with visible diced potato and carrot, short pan handle to the cook right, and one accessible brass-rimmed rotary heat dial on the upper-right front. Replace the entire oven-like lower cabinet with a dedicated stovetop burner: a shallow charcoal cast-iron heating head, 16 units wide by 5 units tall, held at working height on four slim square iron legs with a low simple horizontal brace. Leave a large open negative space beneath the heating head. No oven cavity, oven door, broad hinged front panel, door handle, baking window, decorative instrument or shelf contents. On the upper heating head's front left place just three short narrow horizontal ventilation slots with subtle ember light, not a window or door. Pan height and existing dial pivot are preserved. Reference 2 supplies period Civilization kitchen material language and the SEPARATE baking oven; do not copy its brick shell or door onto this stove. The stove must visibly serve only pan cooking. Native legal Java cuboid geometry, small beveled octagonal dial, economical forms. Authored 64px-per-block pixel-art material density: dark graphite cast iron with quiet tonal clusters, narrow cool steel highlights and small worn edges; brass only on dial rim/pointer. Clean readable silhouette, physically connected pan, head, supports and braces. No text, logos, copper glow, modern gas pipes, giant glowing window or extra controls. Show enough front and right side to judge open stand and pan contents. This is a single selected design, not multiple alternatives.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Refine the surface art of ONE Civilization Minecraft stovetop. Reference 1 gives the selected compact stove shape; preserve shallow cast-iron heating head, open lower stand with four slender legs and low braces, one shallow square skillet at the same working height, short right pan handle, one brass-rimmed upper-right heat dial and four short ventilation slots at front left. Reference 2 shows the bad current in-game materials: overly mottled gray iron reads like stone and the generic grain repeats on every piece. Correct those defects. Reference 3 supplies Civilization kitchen construction language; do not add its separate oven door or brickwork. Render one whole stove front three-quarter view on neutral gray background. Use QUIET charcoal cast iron: broad coherent flat metal tones and sparse fine marks, not speckled granite, rust or gritty camouflage. Apply stove-specific art deliberately: a thin fitted casting seam and worn steel line around the upper heating head, four small steel corner fasteners on each broad housing face; a recessed slim steel surround for the existing four slots; a restrained arc of engraved ticks immediately around the existing single dial, without numbers; thin worn gray iron rim on the skillet, clean near-black cooking well, subtle longitudinal scuffs along straight supporting legs and hardware where braces join. Brass belongs only to the dial, not seams or bolt heads. Existing potato/carrot food remains visible. Detail hierarchy: recognizable masses first, sharp purposeful assembly accents second, very restrained fine 64px-per-block material detail last. One/two-texel fine marks should occupy selected edges and joints, not fill every face with noise. Native cuboid Minecraft model style, exact same bounds and existing functions. No oven cavity, door, handle on the housing, decorative logo, new controls, pressure gauge, gears, added burners, copper glow or extra action. Show all parts joined physically.

criteria.family_consistency: Same quiet dark metal and functional cooking surface as the inspected T1 stove; removes oven detail for this prototype.
criteria.controls_readability: One contrasting upper-right dial with brass pointer, separate lower-left coal window.
criteria.gameplay_scope: Only stove and skillet; no prep table, oven, chimney, extra cooking actions or tools.

criteria.matches_direction: Six actual native views preserve four short feet, shallow 11-unit pan, short right handle, separate coal door and upper-right dial. Simplified shell retains the selected large masses.
criteria.geometry_uvs: Legal native Java cuboids and casting rotations, deliberate 2px/unit regions. Fire-window decal uses an explicit fit region. No floating pan or intersections with rim.
criteria.material_consistency: Original accepted stove iron source throughout; quieter pan interior distinguishes cookware. Brass accents confined to door handle and thin dial rim.
criteria.assembly_interfaces: Single experimental block; top food and front pointer share measured coordinates with renderer. No construction guide or multiblock claimed.
criteria.animation_states: Static shell accepted here; pointer and food are dynamic client geometry and require in-game inspection. No mechanical transmission.
criteria.native_size_readability: Native sheet shows a clear pan opening, front dial ring and fire recess. Small fittings are restrained, not excessive.

criteria.photon_materials: Actual Photon/Faithful display matches the existing T1 Cooking Stove: dark iron with restrained warm fittings. Food is visibly pale, golden or charred; fire emission remains local to its window.
criteria.scale_readability: Single-block cabinet and short feet read beside the original stove. Shallow pan opening remains visible at standing height; varied-height diced food replaces the rejected flat-grid presentation. Brass rim separates the dial from the iron face.
criteria.states_motion: Inspected pale/golden/charred states and fueled cooking. Physical pointer follows continuous settings; actual drag changes the server demand to 83%. Pointer direction matches the menu rotary control. No timer or perfect-state flash.
criteria.interaction_guides: Actual shared cabinet menu shows fixed ingredient quantities, rotary dial, coal/ignition and Load/Serve controls, without clipped status text. Serving locks the batch exactly once. Experimental block has no multiblock guide.
criteria.inventory_appearance: Native inventory shot shows distinct stove shell and warm prepared-meal icon; scale/detail fits the existing item family. No moving-vessel appearance is claimed.
criteria.integration_limits: Hidden guarded client verified rotary input and serving; 254 server tests passed. Sound assets load without missing-event errors and blend from code, but human cue recognition, enjoyment, sound-only mastery and dense-kitchen tuning remain unverified. No Survival recipe or full kitchen construction claimed.
